samples.question: This image shows two open jars standing on the same table line, a left jar and a right jar. The page frame, the table line, the short grey ticks under it, the grey jar walls and the pale grey grid lines are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. The liquid in a jar is the solid coloured block that fills it from the bottom; both jars hold liquid of the same colour. Every jar interior is ruled into identical square cells, and the cells are exactly the same size in the left jar and in the right jar, so the amount of liquid in a jar is the number of coloured cells it contains, counted as width in cells times height in cells. The two jars have different widths and their liquid surfaces stand at different heights. Answer from this image alone, not from the usual expectation that whichever liquid stands higher must be the larger amount. Which jar holds more liquid? Answer with exactly one word: left or right.
